_comment: Mutations that remove the guarantee added by the fix for the $499
'Managed' tier in the PWA: a customer on the Managed tier (or on the
legacy `premium` spelling of it) must never be locked out of a PRO
block or told to upgrade.
The PWA decided the question with
plan === "pro" || plan === "institutional"
which was only correct while "pro" was the top tier. The $499 tier
sits ABOVE Professional, so a customer who paid $499 saw the padlock on
every PRO block in the strategy editor and was told to upgrade.
The PWA receives the RAW plan key: `/users/me` returns the ORM user
unchanged (api/depthsight_api.py:1874) and `User.plan` is a plain
string. The server resolves the legacy `premium` key onto `managed` at
READ time (api/plans.py `resolve_plan_key`) and the rows are NOT
migrated, so 'premium' is a key the PWA really sees -- B covers it.
A is the tier list: without 'managed' in it, a Managed customer is
locked out again. B is the legacy alias: without it, a legacy `premium`
customer is locked out again. C is the decision itself, re-spelled as
the old exact-string comparison. D is the normalisation: the server
strips and lowercases the key, so the client has to agree. E and F are
the two customer-facing call sites, each re-spelled as the old exact-
string comparison. G drops 'institutional', which the helper has always
accepted.
Run with:  python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/pwa_managed_tier_access.json
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.

mutations.label: A: the Managed tier is no longer above Professional
B: the legacy premium key no longer resolves onto managed
C: the gate is the old exact-string comparison again
mutations.needle:
